title: The many lies of PED users (part. 1)
summary: Long monologue aimed at naturals who plan to use PEDs later, debunking the excuses PED users give: 'steroids don't do much', 'it just helps recovery', hyperresponders and 'genetics is everything'. He argues PEDs are 'liquid tonnage' worth about 50 lb of lean mass, that enhanced influencers can't teach naturals, and that PED culture is a death cult.
claims: He attacks PED users' lies, not their freedom: you may do what you want with your body but you are not free from judgment or entitled to make taxpayers pay the medical bills
His real target is naturals planning to juice once they hit their 'natty limit'; if drugs could break that limit, there was no limit, because years of work could have done it
Over 99% of YouTube fitness viewers are natural, yet the biggest channels are run by enhanced lifters, which normalizes drug use
Being natural is the norm statistically and biologically; PED users are outliers who shouldn't be allowed to recast themselves as the new norm
He cannot name one enhanced YouTuber who isn't lying at least a little about how drugs affect their physique or health
Three H's distinguish natural lifters: health, honesty and honor

Pro athletes are effectively forced to use drugs because competitors do; all pro bodybuilders juice, and natural bodybuilding can never match the standard they set, so naturals must be a separate thing
Sports must keep progressing to stay exciting, which is why natural bodybuilding will never reach pro-level spectacle
The loudest online PED advocates are usually naturals who have never used; steroids amplify existing depression and negative traits
He met 15-20 PED users in commercial gyms who were depressed and wanted to quit but felt addicted; none stopped and three have since died
PED dependence works like an abusive relationship or Stockholm syndrome: users defend the drug and get angry at whoever points out the harm
The halo effect makes viewers equate size with knowledge; you can't switch it off, but judge information by logic rather than physique
'Steroids don't do much' is a lie: pros wouldn't all use them and people wouldn't pay for black-market vials and risk felonies if they did little
Pro bodybuilder training looks hard but on paper is mostly fluff: about 80% junk volume, few top sets, far from relevant intensity
He is about 210 lb at 16-17% bodyfat; pros of his height step on stage around 260 lb lean, a roughly 50 lb lean-mass gap no training or diet explains
If training produced that 50 lb, enhanced lifters' tonnage would have to be monstrous, like 5-6 hours a day of top sets; it isn't, so the drugs fill the gap
He cites a study (about five years earlier) where men on 500 mg testosterone without training gained more muscle than naturals training properly; real users take far more for 10-20 years
'Less is more' doesn't refute dose-response: gains keep rising above 500 mg until some threshold most never reach
Training difficulty is defined by numbers on paper (sets, reps, intensity, volume, frequency), not breathlessness or muscle pain
PEDs are 'liquid tonnage': each injection is like weeks of training, so the enhanced can grow lifting around 40% of max while a natural doing that stays small
Low-fat, super-high-protein pro diets may work on drugs but not for naturals; drugs mask bad training and diet
Remove the drug and an enhanced physique collapses; remove the training and it largely maintains, so the drug is the main driver
The pump is useless for growth; pros value it only because it looks good
The hyper/non-responder meme is exaggerated: most PED users who don't grow are lazy, train poorly and diet badly
Illustratively, if natural hormone levels range 80-120, an enhanced lifter sits around 500, four times higher; autopsies find grams of drugs in dead bodybuilders
When a natural is big you see accumulated tonnage; when an enhanced lifter is big you see accumulated drugs
Enhanced influencers spread 'genetics is everything' to level the field and protect their credibility; since naturals have similar hormone levels, natural advice transfers far better
Some people are more gifted, but who cares: you're not competing, aim to be your best, which needs no drugs
An enhanced lifter can't teach naturals how to build delts: if he knew, he'd have built them naturally
PED culture is a death cult disguised as a life cult, selling fame and muscles while hiding depression, guilt and health damage
